quiz.title: Module 2 — Understanding Typography
quiz.description: Monday's quiz covers the purpose of typography, typeface against font, typeface categories, kerning and tracking, legibility, choosing fonts by personality, combining fonts, and common typesetting problems.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of typography in graphic design?
options: To decorate a design without considering its message
To use text as a visual element to communicate a message
To ensure every design uses the same typeface
To replace images in all forms of graphic design
questions.explanation: Typography is communication, not decoration. The words are a visual element chosen and arranged to carry a message to a reader.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a typeface and a font?
options: A typeface describes a family of characters with shared design features, while a font refers to a particular style, weight, and size within that typeface.
A typeface is used only for printed materials, while a font is used only for digital designs.
A typeface refers to the size of letters, while a font refers to their colour.
A typeface contains only uppercase letters, while a font contains only lowercase letters.
questions.explanation: The typeface is the design — the family. A font is one specific cut of it: a given weight, style and size.

questions.prompt: Which typeface category is generally suitable for long-form text, such as books, magazines, and newspapers, because of its legibility?
options: Display fonts
Script fonts
Serif fonts
Decorative fonts
questions.explanation: Serifs guide the eye along a line of text, which is why they hold up over long passages. Display, script and decorative faces are made for short, expressive use.

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between kerning and tracking?
options: Kerning adjusts the space between lines, while tracking adjusts the space between paragraphs.
Kerning adjusts the space between two individual characters, while tracking adjusts spacing across a group of letters.
Kerning changes the font's weight, while tracking changes its height.
Kerning applies only to lowercase text, while tracking applies only to uppercase text.
questions.explanation: Kerning fine-tunes a single pair of letters. Tracking opens or closes the spacing evenly across a whole run of text.

questions.prompt: Which factor can improve the legibility of a typeface when it is displayed at a small size?
options: Using extremely thin strokes
Choosing a highly decorative typeface
Using a typeface with a taller x-height
Increasing the contrast between thick and thin strokes as much as possible
questions.explanation: A taller x-height makes the lowercase letters read larger at the same point size, so the text stays legible when small. Thin strokes and high contrast do the opposite.

questions.prompt: A designer is creating a formal restaurant menu and wants the typography to communicate elegance and sophistication. According to the lesson, what should guide the designer's font selection?
options: The font's personality and whether it suits the content and intended audience
The number of decorative effects available in the font
The designer's preference, regardless of the menu's purpose
The use of as many different typefaces as possible
questions.explanation: Fonts carry personality. The choice should answer to what the design is for and who will read it, not to the designer's taste alone or how many effects a face offers.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a recommended approach to combining fonts in a design?
options: Combine several fonts from the same category that look almost identical.
Use at least five different fonts to make the design visually interesting.
Combine fonts with different characteristics, such as a serif and a sans serif, while keeping the number of fonts limited.
Use decorative fonts for every heading and paragraph.
questions.explanation: Contrast is what makes a pairing work, but the pair still has to get along. Two clearly different faces keep the design readable; a shelf of half-similar ones looks accidental.

questions.prompt: A paragraph contains a single word on the last line, separated from the rest of the paragraph. What is this typesetting problem called?
options: A rag
A widow
A river
An orphan
questions.explanation: A short last line stranded on its own is a widow. An orphan is the opposite — a line stranded at the top of a new page or column.
